one_liner: Senior Executive Service job leading ACF's entire grants management office: grants policy, oversight of risk and audit resolution, grants systems, and the staff who run them.
fit_summary: This SES role requires executive leadership of a large federal grants portfolio. Daniel's grant experience (county COVID-19 grant applications, FEMA Public Assistance onboarding) is relevant context but far from executive level, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public, so federal status is not required, but this is a Senior Executive Service career appointment.
Your two-page resume must show all five Executive Core Qualifications and all three Technical Qualifications. Separate narratives are not accepted.
TQ 1-3 require demonstrated executive-level experience in federal grants management policy, grants operations and organizational leadership, and principal advisory and stakeholder work.
If selected, your qualifications must be certified by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board, and you then serve a one-year probationary period.
No education requirement and no clearance required.
strategy: Skip this one: this SES role requires executive leadership of a large federal grants portfolio, and his grant work (county COVID-19 grant applications, FEMA Public Assistance onboarding) is far from that level.
Target GS-9 to GS-12 grants management specialist or emergency management program roles, where the county grant and FEMA Public Assistance work counts.
resume_bullets: Helped counties update their applications for COVID-19 emergency grants (2020).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets (2019–2020).
interview_questions: Describe how you led a large grants organization through significant change, and how you held people accountable.
How have you applied risk-based approaches and internal controls to prevent improper payments or waste?
Walk us through an audit resolution or corrective action plan you oversaw from finding to closure.
How would you advise ACF leadership on a proposed regulation that affects grantees nationwide?
watch_outs: SES positions almost always require years of senior leadership. Without clear executive-level grants experience, you will likely be rated ineligible.
Anything beyond page 2 of your resume will not be reviewed, and an over-length resume may be disqualified.
Even after selection, OPM QRB certification is required, followed by a one-year probationary period.
The job is located in Washington, DC with telework but is not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas.
